blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

How are deserts formed

A A desert refers to a barren section of land, mainly in arid and semi-arid areas, where there is almost no precipitation and the environment is hostile for any creature to inhabit. Deserts have been classified in a number of ways, generally combining total precipitation, how many days the rainfall occurs, temperature, humidity, and sometimes additional factors. In some places, deserts have clear boundaries marked by rivers, mountains or other landforms, while in other places there are no clear-cut borders between deserts and other landscape features.

B In arid areas where there is no covering of vegetation to protect the land, sand and dust storms frequently take place. This phenomenon often occurs along the desert margins rather than within the deserts, where there is already no finer material left. When a steady wind starts to blow, fine particles on the open ground begin vibrating. As the wind picks up, some of the particles are lifted into the air. When they fall onto the ground, they hit other particles, which are then jerked into the air in their turn, initiating a chain reaction.

C There has been a great deal of publicity about how severe desertification can be, but the academic circle has never agreed on its causes. A common misunderstanding is that a shortage of precipitation causes desertification—yet land in some barren areas will soon recover after rain falls. In fact, more often than not, human activities are responsible. It is widely accepted that the explosion in world population, especially in developing countries, is the primary cause of soil degradation and desertification. As populations become denser, the cultivation of crops has expanded into progressively drier areas. These regions are especially likely to go through periods of severe drought, which explains why crop failures are common. The raising of most crops requires the natural vegetation cover to be removed first; when crop failures occur, extensive tracts of land are left devoid of plant cover and thus susceptible to wind and water erosion. Throughout the 1990s, dry-land areas experienced a population growth of 18.5 per cent, mostly in severely impoverished developing countries.

D Livestock farming in semi-arid areas accelerates soil erosion and becomes one of the reasons for advancing desertification. In such areas, where the vegetation is dominated by grasses, the breeding of livestock is a major economic activity. Grasses are necessary for anchoring barren topsoil in a dry-land area. When a specific field is used to graze an excessive herd, it loses vegetation cover, and the soil is trampled as well as pulverised, leaving the topsoil exposed to destructive forces such as wind and unexpected thunderstorms. For centuries, nomads have grazed their flocks and herds wherever pasture could be found, and oases have offered opportunities for a more settled way of living. For some nomads, wherever they move, the desert follows.

E Trees are of great importance when it comes to maintaining topsoil and slowing down wind speed. In many Asian countries, firewood is the chief fuel used for cooking and heating, which has caused uncontrolled clear-cutting of forests in dry-land ecosystems. When too many trees are cut down, windstorms and dust storms tend to occur.

F What is worse, political conflicts and wars can also contribute to desertification. To escape invading enemies, refugees often move into some of the most vulnerable ecosystems on the planet. They bring along their traditional cultivation practices, which may not be suitable for their new settlements.

G In the 20th century, one state in the United States had a large section of farmland that turned into desert. Since then, measures have been enforced so that such a phenomenon will not happen again. To avoid the recurrence of desertification, people must find livelihoods that do not rely on traditional land uses, are less demanding on local natural resources, yet can still generate viable income. Such livelihoods include, but are not limited to, dry-land aquaculture for the raising of fish, crustaceans and industrial compounds derived from micro-algae, greenhouse agriculture, and activities related to tourism. Another way to prevent desertification is to create economic prospects in the city centres of dry-lands and in areas outside them. Changing the wider economic and institutional structures so that people have new ways to support themselves would help alleviate the pressures that drive desertification.

H In today's society, new technologies are being used to address the problems brought about by desertification. Satellites, for example, have been utilised to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet. However, this does not mean that alternative technologies are not needed to help tackle the processes of desertification.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–20

Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 14–20 on your answer sheet.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFGH
14 a reference to the irregular movement of particles
15 mention of productive land turning into desert in the 20th century
16 types of deserts
17 mention of technical methods used to tackle the problems of deserts
18 the influence of migration on desertification
19 lack of agreement among scientists about the causes of desertification
20 a description of the harmful effects of farming practices

Questions 21–26

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 2?

In boxes 21–26 on your answer sheet, write

  • TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
  • FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
  • NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this

21 It is difficult to ascertain where deserts end in some areas.

22 The media is uninterested in the problems of desertification.

23 The most common cause of desertification is a lack of rainfall.

24 Farming animals in semi-arid areas will increase soil erosion.

25 People in Asian countries no longer use firewood as their chief fuel.

26 Technology for studying the relationship between people, livestock and desertification has not yet been invented.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 沙漠指干旱半干旱地区的荒芜土地，降水稀少，环境恶劣难以栖息。沙漠分类通常结合降水量、降雨天数、温度、湿度等因素，部分沙漠以河流、山脉等地形为明确边界，部分则与其他地貌无清晰分界。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 干旱地区因缺乏植被保护，沙尘暴频发（多发生在沙漠边缘，沙漠内部已无细颗粒物质）。当持续风吹过时，地面细颗粒开始振动，风力增强时部分颗粒被扬起，下落时撞击其他颗粒，引发链式反应，更多颗粒被卷入空中。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 荒漠化的严重性广受关注，但学术界对其成因始终无共识。常见误解认为 “降水不足导致荒漠化”，但荒芜地区雨后常能快速恢复；事实上，人类活动才是主因。全球人口激增（尤其发展中国家）是土壤退化与荒漠化的首要原因 —— 人口密度增加使农作物种植向更干旱地区扩张，这些地区易发生严重干旱，导致农作物频繁歉收；种植作物需先清除自然植被，歉收后土地裸露，易受风力与水力侵蚀。20 世纪 90 年代，干旱地区人口增长 18.5%，且多集中在极度贫困的发展中国家。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 半干旱地区的畜牧业加速土壤侵蚀，是荒漠化加剧的原因之一。这些地区植被以草本植物为主，畜牧业是主要经济活动，而草本植物对固定干旱地区表土至关重要。过度放牧导致植被消失，土壤被践踏粉碎，表土暴露于风沙与暴雨等破坏力之下。数世纪以来，游牧民族随水草迁徙，绿洲为定居生活提供可能，但部分游牧活动所到之处，沙漠随之扩张。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 树木对保持表土、减缓风速至关重要。在许多亚洲国家，木柴是烹饪取暖的主要燃料，导致干旱生态系统的森林被无节制砍伐，树木减少后沙尘暴频发。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 更严重的是，政治冲突与战争也会加剧荒漠化。难民为躲避战乱，常迁入全球最脆弱的生态系统，带入的传统耕作方式可能不适应当地环境，进一步破坏生态。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 20 世纪，美国某州大片农田退化为沙漠，此后相关措施出台以防止类似事件重演。要避免荒漠化，需为居民寻找不依赖传统土地利用、低消耗当地资源且能产生可行收入的生计方式（如干旱地区水产养殖、温室农业、旅游业相关活动）；另一种方法是在干旱地区市中心及周边创造经济机会，通过改革经济与制度结构，为居民提供新的谋生途径，缓解荒漠化驱动压力。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 如今，新技术被用于解决荒漠化问题（如卫星用于研究人类与畜牧业对地球的影响），但这并不意味着无需其他替代技术应对荒漠化进程。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 14–20：Which paragraph contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a reference to the irregular movement of particles（提及颗粒的不规则运动）
答案：B
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “fine particles on the open ground begin vibrating. As the wind picks up, some of the particles are lifted into the air. When they fall onto the ground, they hit other particles, which are then jerked into the air in their turn”，描述颗粒 “振动、被扬起、撞击后不规则跳动”，与题干对应，因此答案为 B。

（2）题目 15：mention of productive land turning into desert in the 20th century（提及 20 世纪可耕地退化为沙漠）
答案：G
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “In the 20th century, one state in the United States had a large section of farmland that turned into desert”，“farmland（农田）” 对应 “productive land（可耕地）”，明确提到 20 世纪可耕地沙化，与题干对应，因此答案为 G。

（3）题目 16：types of deserts（沙漠的类型）
答案：A
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “Deserts have been classified in a number of ways, generally combining total precipitation, how many days the rainfall occurs, temperature, humidity, and sometimes additional factors”，“classified” 对应 “types”，明确提到沙漠的分类（即类型），与题干对应，因此答案为 A。

（4）题目 17：mention of technical methods used to tackle the problems of deserts（提及用于应对沙漠问题的技术方法）
答案：H
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “new technologies are being used to address the problems brought about by desertification. Satellites, for example, have been utilised to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet”，“satellites（卫星）” 对应 “technical methods”，明确提到技术手段的应用，与题干对应，因此答案为 H。

（5）题目 18：the influence of migration on desertification（迁徙对荒漠化的影响）
答案：F
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “To escape invading enemies, refugees often move into some of the most vulnerable ecosystems... They bring along their traditional cultivation practices, which may not be suitable for their new settlements”，“refugees often move（难民迁徙）” 对应 “migration”，明确提到迁徙带来的耕作方式破坏生态，加剧荒漠化，与题干对应，因此答案为 F。

（6）题目 19：lack of agreement among scientists about the causes of desertification（科学家对荒漠化成因的意见分歧）
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “the academic circle has never agreed on its causes”，“academic circle（学术界）” 对应 “scientists”，“never agreed on” 对应 “lack of agreement”，明确提到科学家对成因无共识，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（7）题目 20：a description of the harmful effects of farming practices（描述耕作方式的有害影响）
答案：D
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “When a specific field is used to graze an excessive herd, it loses vegetation cover, and the soil is trampled as well as pulverised, leaving the topsoil exposed to destructive forces such as wind and unexpected thunderstorms”，“grazing an excessive herd（过度放牧）” 对应 “farming practices”，明确描述其导致 “植被消失、土壤裸露” 等危害，与题干对应，因此答案为 D。

items.text:
（1）题目 21：It is difficult to ascertain where deserts end in some areas.（部分地区难以确定沙漠的边界）
题目翻译：部分地区难以确定沙漠的边界。
答案：TRUE（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “in other places there are no clear-cut borders between deserts and other landscape features”，“no clear-cut borders” 对应 “difficult to ascertain where deserts end”，明确提到部分地区沙漠无清晰边界，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 TRUE。

（2）题目 22：The media is uninterested in the problems of desertification.（媒体对荒漠化问题不感兴趣）
题目翻译：媒体对荒漠化问题不感兴趣。
答案：FALSE（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “There has been a great deal of publicity about how severe desertification can be”，“a great deal of publicity” 对应 “media is interested”，明确提到荒漠化问题广受关注（媒体报道多），与题干 “不感兴趣” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 FALSE。

（3）题目 23：The most common cause of desertification is a lack of rainfall.（荒漠化最常见的原因是降水不足）
题目翻译：荒漠化最常见的原因是降水不足。
答案：FALSE（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “A common misunderstanding is that a shortage of precipitation causes desertification-yet land in some barren areas will soon recover after rain falls. In fact, more often than not, human activities are responsible”，明确指出 “降水不足是误解，人类活动才是主因”，与题干 “最常见原因是降水不足” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 FALSE。

（4）题目 24：Farming animals in semi-arid areas will increase soil erosion.（半干旱地区饲养牲畜会加剧土壤侵蚀）
题目翻译：半干旱地区饲养牲畜会加剧土壤侵蚀。
答案：TRUE（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “Livestock farming in semi-arid areas accelerates soil erosion and becomes one of the reasons for advancing desertification”，“accelerates soil erosion” 对应 “increase soil erosion”，明确提到半干旱地区畜牧业加剧土壤侵蚀，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 TRUE。

（5）题目 25：People in Asian countries no longer use firewood as their chief fuel.（亚洲国家的人们不再将木柴作为主要燃料）
题目翻译：亚洲国家的人们不再将木柴作为主要燃料。
答案：FALSE（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “In many Asian countries, firewood is the chief fuel used for cooking and heating”，明确提到亚洲国家仍以木柴为主要燃料，与题干 “不再使用” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 FALSE。

（6）题目 26：Technology for studying the relationship between people, livestock and desertification has not yet been invented.（用于研究人类、牲畜与荒漠化关系的技术尚未发明）
题目翻译：用于研究人类、牲畜与荒漠化关系的技术尚未发明。
答案：FALSE（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “Satellites, for example, have been utilised to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet”，明确提到 “卫星技术已用于研究人类、牲畜与地球（含荒漠化）的关系”，与题干 “尚未发明” 描述矛盾，因此判定为 FALSE。
